primitives.name: Cycle Enrichment Diagnostic
primitives.verbatim_quote: Cycle analysis: 3-cycle density (cycles / all node triads) and cycle-vs-feedforward-loop ratio; cycle *enrichment* = observed 3-cycles vs expected under resampled outcomes from a given ranking score's implied win probabilities.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_{obs}': 'Observed number of 3-cycles in win graph', 'C_{exp}': 'Expected number of 3-cycles under resampled outcomes', 'SD': 'Standard deviation of simulated 3-cycle counts'}
primitives.assumptions: Win graph is constructed from pairwise outcomes; resampling assumes ranking score implies accurate win probabilities.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When observed cycles exceed expected under ranking model, indicates model underestimates parity.

layer2.mapping: Cycle enrichment quantifies deviation from transitive hierarchy; GSE uses this to adjust rating-based win probabilities for parity correction.
layer2.telemetry: Deviation of observed 3-cycle count from expected under resampled win probabilities.

primitives.name: Hierarchy Measures
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Three hierarchy measures on yearly directed win graphs: flow hierarchy (FH), global reaching centrality from 2-reach (GRC/2RC), random-walk hierarchy (RWH/RWC) — compared against configuration-model and Erdős–Rényi null ensembles.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'FH': 'Flow hierarchy value (dimensionless)', 'GRC/2RC': 'Global reaching centrality from 2-reach (dimensionless)', 'RWH/RWC': 'Random-walk hierarchy (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Directed win graphs represent transitive hierarchy; null models assume randomness in edge formation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low values indicate weak hierarchy; high values suggest strong transitivity in outcomes.

layer2.mapping: Hierarchy measures map to network transitivity; GSE uses these to validate structural consistency of win graphs.
layer2.telemetry: Transitivity metrics derived from directed win graph structure.

primitives.name: Prediction Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Prediction protocol: P(A beats B) = f(score_A - score_B) with f fitted per year on trailing data; FM = mean 1[wrong] (0.5 baseline = random); SE = mean (p - outcome)2 (0.25 = random).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'f': 'Mapping function from score difference to win probability', 'FM': 'Fraction of mistakes (dimensionless)', 'SE': 'Average squared error (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Score differences linearly map to win probabilities; errors follow Bernoulli distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When FM approaches 0.5 or SE nears 0.25, model lacks predictive power.

layer2.mapping: Prediction protocol defines model evaluation criteria; GSE applies similar logic to rate match outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: Model accuracy metrics (FM, SE) computed on out-of-sample predictions.

The core insight is that pairwise contests form directed networks where hierarchy can be quantified through multiple metrics—flow hierarchy, centrality-based measures, and random walk methods. These are compared against null models to assess significance. The cycle enrichment diagnostic isolates the extent to which observed 3-cycles deviate from what would be expected under a ranking score’s implied win probabilities. This provides a robust measure of parity and upset potential. In GSI, such diagnostics inform calibration of uncertainty bounds in probabilistic forecasts. In GSE, they guide refinement of state transitions in team performance models by detecting when structural assumptions about transitivity fail. The prediction protocol ensures that models are evaluated using consistent metrics (FM, SE) against baselines like random guessing or official rankings. The failure mode occurs when models overfit to noise or misrepresent transitivity, leading to poor generalization. The key duality lies between structural hierarchy and stochasticity: while hierarchy implies order, cycle enrichment reveals disorder or unpredictability.
